scope: Handshake-wide plugin platform ownership, Studio domain adapters and portable embedding contracts; no implementation or runtime verdict

decision.owner: Existing product-wide manifest, extension-host, capability/consent, sandbox and MEX authorities govern plugins. Do not create a competing Studio registry, library, scheduler, database or permission authority.
decision.implementation_gap: Inspected MEX engine-descriptor registry and trusted EngineAdapter registration are reusable execution seams, not proof of plugin installation, activation, update, uninstall or isolation. Platform lifecycle remains a planned gap requiring explicit owning work before Studio can claim it.
decision.studio: ScorePlugin is the native audio domain adapter. Other Studio extension points use a Studio adapter/projection of the shared platform. Preserve existing Studio extension payloads while correcting ownership.
decision.embedding: Studio modules depend on versioned host-neutral provider ports; the Handshake host binds those ports to its canonical authority. Other hosts supply their own equivalent authority ports and explicitly reject unsupported capabilities; embedding never copies live grants or creates a hidden Handshake database.

required_controls.contract: Manifest identity/version/content digest, supported interface/host versions, permissions and typed contributions bind installed bytes. Quarantine untrusted packages and probe executables only in an authorized bounded isolation provider.

Lifecycle explicitly defines install, verify, activate with current consent, invoke, revoke, drain, update/rollback and uninstall. Lease epochs fence stale completions; accepted durable outcomes reconcile before retirement. No automatic old grant reuse after package or scope change.

Every invocation and restricted receipt lookup rechecks current principal/resource/action authorization and revocation epoch. Declared capabilities and copied granted-capability lists alone are insufficient.

Resource admission charges aggregate executable/module bytes, worker/process/store/instance counts, queued producers/payload bytes, retained generations, devices and reclamation capacity. Reserve cancellation/completion paths; retain permits until actual retirement.

Durable mutations remain host-authority proposals with payload/precondition-bound idempotency, atomic event/receipt commit and current authorization. Plugin private document data follows undo/export/privacy policy; local KV uses canonical scoped authority and contains no secrets or shadow document state.

Versioned ports cover capabilities, jobs/resources, artifacts, document proposals/snapshots, typed errors, UI contributions, observations and manual/recovery help. Ports expose unsupported and partial outcomes explicitly without backend-specific types or authority bypass.

UI uses isolated typed contribution schema, stable namespaced controls and bounded messages; Argus exposes identity/version/state/budgets/errors without secret payloads. Models receive discovery, invocation, cancellation and recovery instructions through the existing product manual.

Native discovery is executable vendor code, not passive metadata reading. Separate bounded isolated probing from activation; record supported crash/hang containment, architecture and ABI negotiation. Never silently fall back to unsafe in-process probing.

Realtime processing forbids blocking, allocation, unbounded command drain, logging, foreign state-save and wrong-thread destruction. State capture is versioned, deadline/byte bounded and explicitly complete/partial/unavailable off callback; reclamation is reserved before transfer.

Update/uninstall cannot invalidate active borrowed code or snapshots. Stop admission, revoke/fence, resolve accepted outcomes, retire instances on permitted threads and release library/store/process resources only after actual quiescence; residual shared-global registries require explicit bounded ownership.

Guest pools and state are partitioned by principal/resource/grant/artifact/state version. Use fresh instances across trust boundaries or independently prove complete reset; retained buffers/state remain classified and charged. Reauthorization occurs before dispatch and output promotion; revoked output cannot become durable authority.

Failed spawn registration, ledger START or decorator state update after actual child creation must retain cleanup ownership or compensate with bounded kill/reap and typed cleanup failure. An error result never implies no live child; shared sandbox owner reconciles actual process lifetime.

Host imports have separate enforced deadlines, cancellation and byte limits; fuel/epoch interruption cannot preempt blocking host code. Bounded chunk/opaque resource protocols avoid arbitrary list copying; unsupported shared-memory/thread/import profiles reject before execution.

Exact closed contribution/event enums and schema negotiation are preserved. Bound asynchronous subscription dispatch, cause depth, replay deduplication and output proposals; never synchronous reentry while host locks are held. Coalesce only replaceable uncommitted previews, never accepted edits or exports.

Native providers require supported OS isolation and approved content-hashed resource paths for discovery and untrusted execution; no ambient directory scan or in-process fallback when unavailable. Preallocated audio bridge declares measured latency, ahead-of-time buffers, deadline bypass/silence policy and quiet UI/headless capability matrix.

Native state capture/restore reports per-instance and per-component/controller phase outcomes. Empty defaults or ignored restoration errors cannot assert completeness; preserve prior required state on capture failure, validate artifact/schema/version and aggregate bytes before promotion.

On revocation, retained private buffers/state MUST be destroyed or rendered inaccessible within a bounded retirement deadline, including idle pools; already-copied bytes cannot be revoked by a capability-list change alone. Permits remain charged until confirmed retirement.

Native editor embedding, accessibility and Argus inspection MUST be separate host-matrix entries from DSP/headless control. Unsupported foreign UI MUST be explicit; automated invocation MUST NOT raise vendor windows.

Every planned platform and Studio module foundation MUST expose its executable minimum before domain feature implementation. Second-host proof establishes portability only and MUST NOT replace independent production Handshake authorization, sandbox, canonical state and Argus/UserManual acceptance.

independent_review.disposition: Independent actual reread confirms PLATFORM17-19 incorporate COR01/COR03/COR07 verbatim; contract review complete; no runtime verdict. Only report binding metadata updated after this reviewed revision.

source_chains.observed: MexRegistry loads mechanical_engines.json into engine/operation maps. Workflow construction installs shell, media downloader and calendar sync adapters. This is engine registration, not an installed plugin manifest/version lifecycle.

EngineAdapter is a trusted async invoke trait. Runtime checks gates then directly awaits the selected adapter. Shell delegates to TerminalService with timeout/output limits and capability context. Generic adapter isolation and deadline cancellation do not follow solely from this trait or BudgetGate.

GatedMcpClient resolves configured tools, checks shared capabilities and consent/session grants. Unknown tools are denied; alias ambiguity errors. Tool discovery is not install/update/remove ownership, and gate admission is not executable sandbox proof.

Shared adapters expose spawn/exec/fs_bind/net_policy/kill. ProcessSpec carries binds/network/resources/caps. Optional resource limits may be None/unlimited. Registry rejects unapproved Windows native jail selection. LedgerDecorator spawns first then writes START; failed recording returns error without a compensating kill in this inspected path.

Authority API describes shared account/principal/session/AccessSpace/capability/grant ResourceBroker boundaries and delegates protected-resource authorization. Native EditorSurface seam explicitly labels itself a design-only stub with no existing runtime caller. Complete installed plugin UI, inspection and manual contribution registration is not established by these excerpts.

primary_research.claim: Native Rust ABI no stability guarantees; explicit external ABI is separate.
WIT worlds imports/exports and owned/borrowed resources define interfaces; they do not authorize resources or guarantee realtime behavior.
Guest access depends on host imports; host policy remains part of security.
Store lifetime retains instances; resource limits and execution interruption are separate controls.
ResourceLimiter does not account all runtime/embedder memory or CPU; shared-memory growth is a limitation; explicitly set resource counts rather than defaults.
Component API distinct from core modules; WIT bindgen generated host traits/types and gated features.
Fuel deterministic with overhead; epoch interruption nondeterministic; trapping and yielding have different semantics.
Init/destroy/activate/deactivate main-thread; start/stop/process audio-thread with state constraints.
Component/controller persistence sequencing, configuration/activation/processing lifecycle and main/audio threading requirements.

findings.quote: Every planned platform and Studio foundation MUST expose its executable minimum before domain features begin
findings.finding: Unqualified platform-foundation plus actual-production proof wording can gate all pure asset domain development on the unfinished shared host lifecycle, contrary to explicit operator phase scope and STU-ARC-006.
findings.correction: Require executable portable platform/provider adapter minima with bounded supported/unsupported consumer paths in the asset foundation barrier. Real shared host install/consent/activate/revoke/lifecycle and production authorization/sandbox/state/Argus/UserManual proof are hard predecessors for actual plugin activation and corresponding host embedding, not unrelated pure asset feature development. HSK-PLG-001 missing lifecycle remains real and is not waived.

findings.quote: Use clean realms across trust boundaries
findings.finding: This names account/resource isolation but does not explicitly prevent same-document repeated evaluations from carrying mutated prototypes/global/closure/host state across ticks. MOT076 separately forbids evaluation-order dependence, so explicit provider control is required.
findings.correction: Require fresh evaluation state for each independent sample/evaluation or independently proven complete reset isolating all mutable globals/prototypes/closures/host memoization. Immutable trusted compiled artifacts may be reused; retries share allowance and exact immutable inputs. Same-document/same-account reversed frame order and fresh-versus-reused worker must conform, not merely cross-account tests.

findings.finding: Acceptance is ambiguous beside CON014 selection/proposal/rejection events which expressly do not claim document promotion. A consumer can require PromotionDecision Accepted and omit proposal/rejection audit events, or emit undurable view telemetry as accepted business authority.
findings.correction: Define the boundary by event class: accepted document mutations mirror only after canonical promotion/event transaction; proposal/rejection/view audit business events mirror only after their own canonical typed record/event is durably accepted, without implying document promotion. Transient uncommitted previews remain distinct bounded diagnostics; same durable mirror-intent/retry/collision controls apply to all required business rows.

final_root_normative_review.supported: All six original openchallenge corrections are represented in CON011/013/014. Exact22 business rows preserve wire identities and existing dot-family vocabulary; planned Studio recorder category explicitly remains unimplemented. MOT258 names MotionJS parser/AST/checkpoint ownership, trusted cache identity, constructor/prototype hostile proof, single-owner reclamation and conversion budgets; source-only/runtime distinctions remain explicit.
